title: docs: HARDENING.md and production-readiness.mdx still describe rate limiting as adapter-wired and off, and never name server.security.rateLimit or trustProxy
body:
Filing gate **③ a task the maintainer set**, in the `repo:hotcrm` seat 2 chat on 2026-10-20 (verbatim): 「docs/HARDENING.md 里的限流配方引用了已经不存在的代码」. Filed by the `repo:hotcrm` seat 2 (`os-support-ai`, session `session_01KqkTQNLcxVc588eZpJmp1r`, seat post objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2180). ⛔ Not a claim. Domain, type and grade are triage's.

**A correction to the order's wording, on measurement:** the symbols the recipe imports still exist. `RateLimiter` and `DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS` are in `packages/runtime/src/security/rate-limit.ts`, exported from `@objectstack/runtime`. What is false is what the two pages say about the runtime, since #4910 wired the built-in limiter. The seat reported this correction to the maintainer when filing.

**Reader (who acts):** objectstack triage routes it to the owner of `docs/` and `content/docs/deployment/`. It is the docs follow-up #4937 did not reach.

## What is false (read on objectstack `main` `9b2953d62`)

`docs/HARDENING.md` § Rate limiting:
- "The runtime exposes a token-bucket primitive but does **not** auto-wire it into the dispatcher plugin … the decision to enable belongs at the adapter layer." **False since #4910.** `createDispatcherPlugin({ rateLimit })` installs the inbound limiter as global middleware from the authored `server.security.rateLimit` block, and `objectstack serve` forwards it. `rate-limit.ts`'s own header and `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` ("The dispatcher plugin wires BOTH automatically") say so.
- § Trust the proxy or don't: "The dispatcher's default key extractor reads `x-forwarded-for[0]`". **False.** `resolveRateLimitKey` (`inbound-rate-limit.ts`) keys on the principal first. It reads forwarded headers only under `server.trustProxy`, and otherwise uses the transport peer.
- The Hono recipe keys its buckets on `x-forwarded-for`'s first entry, unconditionally. That is the client-influenced key the runtime's own resolver refuses without `trustProxy`. A reader who copies it gets a weaker limiter than the one the runtime already ships.
- "For multi-instance deploys, replace the default `MemoryStore` with a Redis-backed `RateLimitStore`." The built-in limiter already counts in the kernel `cache` service (shared when that is Redis), and warns when it falls back to per-process.
- The page never names `server.security.rateLimit` or `trustProxy`, the two keys an operator actually sets. They are documented only in `content/docs/references/system/stack-server.mdx`.

`content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx` (published):
- The defaults table says rate limiting is "Off (opt-in via adapter)".
- The prose says "Rate limiting is the one piece you wire at the adapter layer … See the HARDENING.md recipes".
- The go-live checklist says "Rate limit configured at the adapter for `/auth/*` …".

All three send a reader past the built-in limiter. The published page matters more, because it ships to every operator.

The same `HARDENING.md`'s CORS section ("not opinionated by the runtime") is carried by the CORS card filed alongside this one, not here.

## Expected (proposed; triage owns it)

- Both pages say that rate limiting is built in and off by default. They name `server.security.rateLimit` with an example budget, `server.trustProxy` with when to set it, and the shared-cache requirement for multi-node.
- The adapter recipe is either deleted or kept only as "per-class budgets, which the built-in single bucket does not do", using the runtime's trust rule for its key.
- The go-live checklist points at the built-in key.

## Dedupe (objectstack issues, all states, semantic search)

"HARDENING.md rate limiting recipe stale adapter layer server.security.rateLimit production-readiness docs": 3 hits, all closed.
- #4937 fixed `rate-limit.ts`'s comments.
- #4686 was the ADR-0049 `RateLimitConfig` retirement.
- #5554 fixed `SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s L3 claims.

None covers these two pages.

Dedupe words: HARDENING.md rate limiting stale; production-readiness rate limit adapter; server.security.rateLimit docs; x-forwarded-for recipe.
